title: Compact routing at stretch 2k−1 and n^(1/k) storage
formal: For every integer k≥2, do universal graph-routing schemes exist with stretch at most 2k−1 and Õ(n^(1/k)) words of routing information per vertex, without a preliminary handshake?
definitions: A routing scheme preprocesses a connected undirected weighted graph and assigns local routing tables and destination labels. During a route, each vertex chooses an outgoing port using only its local table, the destination label and a bounded packet header. Stretch bounds routed length divided by shortest-path distance for every ordered pair. The intended model permits topology-dependent labels; it is not name-independent routing, and a global distance oracle alone is insufficient.

context_blocks.text: Compact routing asks how much global network knowledge must be stored locally to deliver paths close to shortest. The proposed space-stretch curve is a central target connecting routing with sparse distance representations.

Chechik improves the achievable stretch in this storage range while retaining a gap to 2k−1. The existing TCS-5770 instead extracts an extremal girth-construction question; that graph-existence target does not provide routing tables, labels or packet forwarding.

why: Reach a basic space-versus-route-quality frontier for distributed network representations.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated proposition or its logical negation, with the specified quantifiers, model and guarantees. A conditional theorem settles only that conditional claim. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof-assistant-checked proof of the full target.
